customManagers.description: just, pinned through taiki-e/install-action's tool input in .github/actions/setup-tools. Renovate's github-actions manager reads that action's own version but not the tool it installs.

packageRules.description: Keep gitleaks in lockstep across scripts/install_pkgs.sh (github-releases) and .pre-commit-config.yaml (pre-commit manager).

Keep just in lockstep across scripts/install_pkgs.sh (cloud sessions) and .github/actions/setup-tools/action.yml (CI); both regex managers name it casey/just. tools/test_python_suites.py fails when they differ, since the `just --dry-run` text check-flash-recipes reads can change between releases.

Hold sphinx below 9.2 in the robocar simulation: sphinx 9.2 requires Python >=3.13 while the simulation's requires-python floor is 3.12, so uv cannot resolve. Drop once the simulation floor moves to 3.13.

Keep torch and torchvision together in melody-train: each torchvision release pins one exact torch (0.28.0 requires torch==2.13.0), so a torch-only bump in the grouped non-major PR makes the train extra unsatisfiable (#895). Renovate does not bump torch here; move it by hand in the PR that bumps torchvision, as #891 did.

Do not bump the espressif/idf base image in the Dockerfile. CI builds firmware with the IDF_VERSION env value in _ci-build-esp32.yml, build-firmware.yml and refresh-idf-locks.yml (plain values Renovate does not manage), and the Kconfig symbol list and resolved partition tables are regenerated per version, so the dev container moves with them as a deliberate ESP-IDF upgrade (#734). docker-compose.yml's mcu-tinkering-lab/esp-idf image tag and versioned esp-idf-tools volume are local names and also stay manual; test_kconfig_symbols.py fails when any of these disagree.

Only patch bumps for the actions/setup-python python-version input (github-actions manager, depType uses-with, depName python, packageName actions/python-versions). A new Python minor can lack wheels for torch and other deps, so moving to one is a deliberate change, not a Renovate PR (#796).

Leave requires-python alone: it is each project's supported-interpreter floor, not a dependency. Pinned to one exact interpreter (#610), it failed every job and machine whose Python differed by a patch, and each Python release reopened the line (#735).
